campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered an interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with public hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The Council also considered authorizing a grant application through the One Bay Area Grant program and reviewing new consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation
Revocation of business license and tobacco permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
One Bay Area Grant application for public works funding
Approval of new consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered adopting a resolution declaring the city's intent to identify specific properties designated under a city program, as a first step in a formal process. The council also considered setting a public hearing for June 17, 2026, where property owners or residents could raise protests before the city moves toward final approval.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Setting June 17, 2026 as the date for a public hearing
Process for residents to file protests
Steps toward final approval of the designation

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up routine business at this meeting, including approval of minutes from two prior meetings and several contract renewals or amendments for town services. The council also considered authorizing the year's library book purchases and reviewed the town's monthly financial report.
keyTopics: Approval of June 16 and June 23, 2026 council meeting minutes
Amendment to the town's tree care services agreement with Brightview
Amendment to the town's legal services contract
Authorization to purchase library books and materials from Ingram for the fiscal year
Review of the monthly financial and investment report

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 12, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to plan upcoming City Council meeting agendas, reviewing the final agenda for August 18, 2026 and the draft agenda for August 25, 2026. Committee members considered adding new items, scheduling specific 'time certain' slots for agenda items, and checking whether any items needed a waiver of standard notice requirements. The committee also discussed a release date for an upcoming study session and reviewed the City Manager's monthly report of activities.
keyTopics: Finalizing the August 18, 2026 City Council agenda
Drafting the August 25, 2026 City Council agenda
Assigning 'time certain' scheduling to specific agenda items
Reviewing waiver requirements for agenda items or documents
Setting a release date for an upcoming City Manager study session

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to discuss several honorary proclamations, including one for National Immigrant Heritage Month and one marking City Attorney Jennifer Logue's appointment to the judiciary, alongside routine financial and infrastructure business. Council also considered the city's annual spending limits and budget policy updates, a five-year water management plan, and next year's capital improvement projects, plus closed-session discussion of potential litigation exposure. Additional items covered repaving Shoreline Golf Links' parking lot, work on the Public Safety Building project, and the South Bay Salt Pond Restoration project.
keyTopics: Proclamations for National Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judicial appointment
Fiscal Year 2026-27 annual appropriations limit and updates to the city's financial and budgetary policy
Adoption of the 5-Year Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan
Recommended Fiscal Year 2026-27 Capital Improvement Program, including the Public Safety Building and Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving
Closed-session discussion of anticipated litigation and the South Bay Salt Pond Restoration project

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: On July 28, 2026, the Sunnyvale City Council met in two parts: a closed session to discuss confidential matters not open to the public, followed by a study session where the Council considered an update on the city's policy for artificial turf. The study session gave Council members a chance to review findings and provide direction before any formal policy decisions are made.
keyTopics: Closed session (confidential city business, not open to the public)
Artificial turf policy study update
Council discussion on guidelines or standards for artificial turf use in Sunnyvale

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event, a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, and a presentation from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The Commission also considered approval of its June 10, 2026 meeting minutes and held time for public comments on non-agenda items.
keyTopics: Planning for the upcoming Bike Fest
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program discussion
Presentation by youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes
Open public comment period for non-agenda items

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Station Area Task Force — July 16, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara Station Area Task Force met on July 16, 2026, with the agenda largely covering standard procedural disclosures rather than new substantive proposals. The main content included legal notices about deadlines for challenging any official decisions made at the meeting, rather than details on specific station area development plans.
keyTopics: Legal disclosure on the 90-day deadline to file lawsuits challenging quasi-adjudicative decisions
Reference to Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure governing legal challenge timelines
Procedural notices standard to Station Area Task Force meetings

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on an upcoming ballot, which would shift the city's business tax structure to a tiered gross receipts model. The proposal was framed around making taxes more closely tied to actual business revenue, protecting small businesses (about 85% of local businesses would see minimal impact), and keeping Milpitas competitive with other cities' tax revenues.
keyTopics: Resolution to submit a Business Tax Modernization Measure to voters
Shift from current business tax structure to a tiered gross receipts tax
Protections and impact analysis for small businesses
Comparison of projected revenue per resident/business against other cities
Simplifying tax administration and adapting to changes in the economy, including tech and new business types

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — June 29, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council held a public hearing on a proposal for 2468 South Court, where the applicant sought approval to tear down an existing one-story house and detached garage and replace them with a new two-story, single-family home of about 2,481 square feet plus a basement. The council reviewed the design under the city's Individual Review process, since a neighbor or party had requested the Director's decision be reconsidered by the council rather than finalized administratively.
keyTopics: Director's Review appeal of a house redesign at 2468 South Court
Demolition of an existing single-story home and detached garage
Plans for a new two-story house with a basement and an attached junior accessory dwelling unit (JADU)
Compliance with R-1 single-family zoning standards
Environmental exemption under state CEQA rules for the project
